note: The description follows Sands's (1965) revision (the species was originally described from a single soldier in 1956; the alate is described here for the first time and the soldier measurements are supplemented), in English; the alate and soldier are included, with no separate worker. The OCR misread decimal points as hyphens (e.g. I-08 for 1.08), restored here.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Larger than M. sorex and M. giffardii, head width (across the eyes) 1.08—1.12, pronotum width 1.25—1.35 and wider than the head width; alate compound eyes rather small (eye width index 3.1—3.6), the bristles of the head and pronotum very dense and even, forming a fur.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, postclypeus brown, antennae and labrum yellowish brown; pronotum, meso- and metanota dark brown, the anterior half of the pronotum with a conspicuous large pale T-shaped mark in the middle, the other thoracic sclerites brown, legs yellowish brown; abdominal tergites dark brown, sternites brown with a paler median line; wing membrane translucent pale brown, the veins dark brown. Posterior margin of the head capsule broadly rounded behind the eyes and slightly convex at the ocular margin; frontal marks pale, narrowing fissures; compound eyes hardly projecting beyond the sides of the head, short-oval and slightly angular, small to medium relative to the head width, eye width index 3.1—3.6; ocelli medium-sized, 1/2—4/5 of their own least diameter from the compound eyes; anterior margin of the postclypeus undulate and convex in the middle, the posterior margin convex and rounded, the width 1.8—1.9 times the length; antennae 15-segmented, segments IV and V nearly equal, II shorter and narrower, III very small. Pronotum very large and shield-shaped, wider than the head width. Head bristles dark brown, extremely dense, short and even, forming a fur, with a few longer outstanding bristles in pairs or groups arranged almost symmetrically, and usually 1 very prominent bristle between each compound eye, ocellus and antennal base. Measurements (10 specimens, 1 locality, mm): head width (across the eyes) 1.08—1.12 (mean 1.10); greatest compound eye diameter 0.30—0.35 (mean 0.33); ocellus 0.10—0.12 × 0.13—0.15 (mean 0.11 × 0.14); ocellus to eye 0.06—0.08 (mean 0.07); pronotum width 1.25—1.35; pronotum length 1.04—1.15 (mean 1.10); hind tibia length 1.00—1.06 (mean 1.04); fore wing length 10.60—11.30 (mean 10.87).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Measurements only; the morphology agrees with the description of the 1956 type specimen, and the new material extends the range of size variation. Measurements (15 specimens, 3 localities, mm): head length (to the tip of the nasus) 1.22—1.61 (mean 1.43); head width 0.82—1.02 (mean 0.94); head capsule depth 0.49—0.64 (mean 0.58); pronotum width 0.43—0.51 (mean 0.47); pronotum length 0.18—0.25 (mean 0.21); hind tibia length 0.59—0.77 (mean 0.67).
